steps.mistake: Boring the liners oversize on the assumption that oversize pistons will be available leaves a block with no factory pistons to fit it.

mistakes.title: Boring liners for oversize pistons
mistakes.what: Boring the liners oversize on the assumption that oversize pistons can be bought.
mistakes.consequence: JLR lists one piston size, so the bored block has no factory pistons to suit and may be scrap.
mistakes.prevent: Confirm piston supply before any machining, and plan a new block or specialist sleeving for a bore beyond limits.

mistakes.title: Not washing out honing grit
mistakes.what: Honing the bores and only wiping them with a rag or solvent.
mistakes.consequence: Abrasive left in the crosshatch wears the new rings and gets into the bearings.
mistakes.prevent: Scrub each bore with hot soapy water until a clean white rag stays clean, then oil it.
mistakes.detect: A white rag wiped through the bore comes out gray.

steps.title: Decide on the crankshaft
steps.action: If journals are within limits, fit graded shells; if scored or out of limits, replace the crankshaft.
steps.why: JLR sizes clearances with graded bearings rather than undersize shells, so a reground crank needs non-factory bearings.

mistakes.title: Regrinding without a bearing plan
mistakes.what: Regrinding the crank before checking that bearings are available for it.
mistakes.consequence: JLR uses graded standard shells, not undersizes, so the reground crank may have no bearings to suit.
mistakes.prevent: Confirm a non-factory undersize bearing source and measure the housings before any grinding, or replace the crank.

steps.title: Select bearing grades
steps.action: Use the crank codes and the block or rod references with JLR's selection charts to pick a color- and letter-coded shell for each journal.
steps.mistake: Ordering one standard size for every journal instead of grading each one.

mistakes.title: Using one shell size for every journal
mistakes.what: Ordering a single standard bearing size for all the journals.
mistakes.consequence: Clearances then vary from journal to journal, so some run tight and some loose, risking a spun or worn bearing.
mistakes.prevent: Grade each main and rod journal separately from the codes and the JLR selection chart.

mistakes.title: Swapping graded upper and lower shells
mistakes.what: Fitting the two halves of a graded pair in each other's positions.
mistakes.consequence: Clearance and oil feed differ from what the chart intended, and a grooved shell in a plain position starves the journal.
mistakes.prevent: Lay out each journal's pair in order with its code and fit them exactly as the chart says.

steps.title: Chase threads and do a final wash
steps.action: Clean all threads, including the drive plate holes with an M10 x 1.0 bottoming tap no deeper than the hole, then wash the block and head and blow them dry.
steps.why: Head and drive plate bolts are torqued to an angle and must go into clean, dry threads.

spec.note: maximum tap depth in drive plate bolt holes

mistakes.title: Tapping drive plate holes too deep
mistakes.what: Running the M10 x 1.0 tap to the bottom of the drive plate bolt holes or beyond the depth limit.
mistakes.consequence: JLR limits the tap depth; going deeper can damage the threads the bolts rely on.
mistakes.prevent: Mark the tap at the limit and use a bottoming tap only to that depth.

mistakes.title: Leaving liquid in blind bolt holes
mistakes.what: Leaving water, solvent or oil in the head bolt holes after washing.
mistakes.consequence: Liquid in a blind hole stops the bolt from seating, gives a false torque reading and can crack the block.
mistakes.prevent: Blow out every blind hole until it is completely dry.

mistakes.title: Skipping the final wash
mistakes.what: Sending the block straight to assembly after machining and thread chasing.
mistakes.consequence: Machining chips and grit are sealed into the engine and embed in the bearings.
mistakes.prevent: Wash the block and head again after all machining and before assembly.

steps.title: Fit and time the balancers
steps.action: Install the outer races if replaced, slide both balancer shafts into their bores, fit the idler gear, and set them in phase with the JLR alignment tools.
steps.why: Out-of-phase balancers add vibration instead of canceling it, and their timing cannot be set once the crank is in.
steps.mistake: Fitting the balancers without the alignment tools and guessing the gear mesh.

mistakes.title: Guessing the balancer gear mesh
mistakes.what: Fitting and meshing the balancer shafts by eye without the alignment tools.
mistakes.consequence: Out-of-phase balancers add vibration rather than canceling it, and correcting it means taking the crank back out.
mistakes.prevent: Use the JLR balancer alignment tools to set both shafts before the crank goes in.

mistakes.title: Fitting the balancers dry
mistakes.what: Sliding the balancer shafts into their bores without oil on the needle bearings.
mistakes.consequence: The bearings run dry on first start and wear early.
mistakes.prevent: Oil the needle bearings and races before sliding the shafts in.

mistakes.title: Fitting the crank before the balancers
mistakes.what: Laying the crankshaft in before the balancers are timed.
mistakes.consequence: The balancer timing can no longer be set, so the crank has to come out again.
mistakes.prevent: Fit and time both balancers first, then fit the crank.

steps.title: Fit the upper main shells
steps.action: Lay the grooved upper main shells, with their oil holes lined up, into the clean, dry block saddles.
steps.why: The block-side shells carry the oil feed to the crank; a cap-side shell in the block starves the journal.
steps.mistake: Mixing up block-side shells with the plain cap-side shells.

mistakes.title: Swapping block and cap shells
mistakes.what: Fitting plain cap-side shells to the block saddles and grooved block-side shells to the caps.
mistakes.consequence: The plain shell covers the block oil feed, so the journal gets no oil and the bearing seizes.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the grooved shells with oil holes to the block and the plain shells to caps 1 to 4.

mistakes.title: Oiling behind the main shells
mistakes.what: Oiling the block saddles or shell backs, or not wiping them dry.
mistakes.consequence: Oil behind a shell spoils heat transfer and shell seating, leading to early bearing failure.
mistakes.prevent: Fit shells to clean, dry saddles and oil only the running face.

mistakes.title: Dirt trapped under a shell
mistakes.what: Leaving a speck of grit on the saddle or shell back.
mistakes.consequence: The trapped grit raises a high spot that rubs the journal and breaks down the bearing lining.
mistakes.prevent: Wipe every saddle and shell back just before fitting and look along it in good light.
mistakes.detect: A localized shiny spot on the Plastigage check.

mistakes.title: Shell oil holes not lined up
mistakes.what: Fitting an upper shell so its oil hole only partly meets the block feed hole.
mistakes.consequence: The journal gets too little oil and the bearing can seize or spin.
mistakes.prevent: Check that each oil hole lines up with its feed before the crank goes in.

steps.title: Fit the thrust washers
steps.action: Place the two thrust washers on either side of the center main web, with their grooves facing the crank.

mistakes.title: Thrust washers fitted backwards
mistakes.what: Fitting the thrust washers with their oil grooves facing the block instead of the crank.
mistakes.consequence: The thrust faces run without an oil film and wear quickly, increasing end play.
mistakes.prevent: Fit both washers with the grooves facing the crankshaft.

mistakes.title: Letting a thrust washer slip out
mistakes.what: Letting a thrust washer slide out of place as the crank is lowered in.
mistakes.consequence: End play is uncontrolled and the crank thrust face wears.
mistakes.prevent: Hold the washers in place with assembly lube and check that both are seated before fitting the caps.

steps.title: Lay in the crankshaft
steps.action: Oil the shells and lower the crankshaft in, meshing its balancer drive gear with the balancer gears.

mistakes.title: Laying the crank in on dry shells
mistakes.what: Fitting the crank without oiling the shell running faces.
mistakes.consequence: The bearings run dry for the first seconds of cranking and are scuffed.
mistakes.prevent: Oil the running face of every shell before the crank goes in.

mistakes.title: Disturbing the balancer timing
mistakes.what: Moving the balancer gears off their timed position while meshing the crank gear.
mistakes.consequence: The balancers run out of phase and add vibration instead of canceling it.
mistakes.prevent: Keep the balancer alignment tools in place until the crank gear is meshed, then confirm the timing.

steps.title: Fit the lower main shells
steps.action: Fit the plain shells to caps 1 to 4 and the partly grooved shell to the rear cap 5.

mistakes.title: Grooved shell in the wrong cap
mistakes.what: Fitting the partly grooved lower shell to a cap other than number 5.
mistakes.consequence: The bearing load area is reduced where a plain shell belongs, and number 5 loses its intended oil flow.
mistakes.prevent: Fit plain shells to caps 1 to 4 and the partly grooved shell to cap 5.

mistakes.title: Shell not flush at the parting faces
mistakes.what: Fitting a shell so it stands proud of one parting face.
mistakes.consequence: Crush is uneven, so the bearing distorts or can spin.
mistakes.prevent: Check that each shell sits evenly in its cap before fitting.

steps.title: Install the main caps
steps.action: Fit each cap to its numbered position with the arrow toward the front of the engine.
steps.mistake: Fitting a cap reversed, which changes the bore geometry and seizes the bearing.

mistakes.title: Main cap fitted backwards
mistakes.what: Fitting a main cap with its arrow pointing at the transmission end.
mistakes.consequence: The bore geometry changes, the bearing clearance closes up and the bearing can seize.
mistakes.prevent: Check that every cap arrow points to the front before fitting its bolts.

mistakes.title: Main caps in the wrong positions
mistakes.what: Fitting the caps in the wrong numbered positions.
mistakes.consequence: Each cap is machined with the block, so a swapped cap misaligns the bore and wipes the bearings.
mistakes.prevent: Fit caps by number and arrow and check the crank turns freely after each is torqued.

steps.title: Torque the main cap bolts
steps.action: Tighten the ten main cap bolts in stages to the JLR value and angle, working from the center out.
steps.why: No published value could be verified for this engine, so take it from the JLR workshop manual.

mistakes.title: Using an unverified main bolt torque
mistakes.what: Using a main cap torque found online instead of the JLR value.
mistakes.consequence: Low clamp lets the caps shift and the bearings fail; too high can stretch the bolts or distort the bores.
mistakes.prevent: Take the main cap torque and angle from the JLR manual, not from a forum or another engine.

mistakes.title: Reusing angle-tightened main bolts
mistakes.what: Reusing the main cap bolts without checking whether JLR calls them single use.
mistakes.consequence: A bolt already taken past yield cannot give reliable clamp load again.
mistakes.prevent: Check the manual and fit new bolts if they are torque-to-yield.

mistakes.title: Wrong lubricant on main bolt threads
mistakes.what: Oiling the bolt threads or leaving them dry without checking the specification.
mistakes.consequence: Clamp load can vary by around 15 percent with the lubricant alone, so the caps end up over- or under-clamped.
mistakes.prevent: Prepare the threads exactly as the manual states, then tighten in stages.

mistakes.title: Tightening mains out of sequence
mistakes.what: Tightening the main bolts from one end, or fully one at a time.
mistakes.consequence: The caps seat unevenly and can pull the bearing bores out of line, so the crank binds.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten in stages from the center outward, then apply the angle in the same order.

steps.title: Check end play and rotation
steps.action: Check crankshaft end play with a dial indicator and turn the crank by hand to confirm it spins freely.

mistakes.title: Not turning the crank by hand
mistakes.what: Torquing the crank in and leaving it without turning it.
mistakes.consequence: A tight spot from a misfitted shell or cap goes unnoticed until the engine runs.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the crank a full turn by hand after each cap is torqued and find any tight spot before going on.

mistakes.title: Measuring end play without seating the thrust
mistakes.what: Reading end play without first pushing the crank fully one way.
mistakes.consequence: The reading is wrong and an out-of-limit thrust clearance is missed.
mistakes.prevent: Lever the crank fully forward and then fully back, with the dial indicator zeroed in between.

steps.title: Assemble pistons to rods
steps.action: Join each piston to its rod with the piston pin and two new circlips, keeping the crown arrow and rod orientation correct.

mistakes.title: Reusing piston pin circlips
mistakes.what: Refitting the circlips removed at teardown to the piston pins.
mistakes.consequence: A weakened clip can come out, letting the pin walk and score the bore.
mistakes.prevent: Fit two new circlips to every piston and never reuse a removed one.

mistakes.title: Circlip not seated in its groove
mistakes.what: Leaving a circlip partly out of its groove.
mistakes.consequence: The clip comes out in service and the pin gouges the liner.
mistakes.prevent: Turn each clip in its groove and check that it is fully seated all the way around.

mistakes.title: Rod and piston paired the wrong way
mistakes.what: Facing the piston arrow forward but turning the rod the wrong way around on the pin.
mistakes.consequence: The rod's features face the wrong way, risking poor bearing oiling and fit.
mistakes.prevent: Check the rod and piston orientation marks together before fitting the pin.

steps.title: Fit and stagger the rings
steps.action: Install the oil control ring, then the two compression rings, and turn them so the gaps are 120 degrees apart.

spec.note: spacing between the three ring gaps

mistakes.title: Rings fitted upside down
mistakes.what: Fitting a compression ring with its top mark facing down.
mistakes.consequence: The ring pumps oil into the chamber, giving oil consumption and smoke.
mistakes.prevent: Fit every marked ring with the mark toward the crown.

mistakes.title: Spiraling rings onto the piston
mistakes.what: Winding rings on by hand instead of using a ring expander.
mistakes.consequence: Thin modern rings bend or twist and no longer seal.
mistakes.prevent: Use a ring expander and open each ring only enough to clear the piston.

mistakes.title: Leaving ring gaps lined up
mistakes.what: Leaving the ring gaps where they fell or lined up with each other.
mistakes.consequence: Aligned gaps give a direct blow-by path and poor compression.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the three gaps 120 degrees apart as JLR specifies.

mistakes.title: Oil ring expander ends overlapped
mistakes.what: Overlapping the oil ring expander ends or catching them in the drain-back slot.
mistakes.consequence: The oil ring does not control oil, causing consumption.
mistakes.prevent: Check that the expander ends butt correctly before fitting the rails.

steps.title: Refit piston cooling jets
steps.action: Bolt the four piston cooling jets back into the block and check that each one points at the underside of its piston.

mistakes.title: Bending a piston cooling jet
mistakes.what: Bending a cooling jet while fitting it, or not aiming it at its piston.
mistakes.consequence: Oil misses the piston underside, which overheats.
mistakes.prevent: Check that each jet nozzle is straight and points at its piston before fitting the pistons.

mistakes.title: Debris in a jet orifice
mistakes.what: Refitting a jet without checking that its small orifice is clear.
mistakes.consequence: A blocked jet stops cooling one piston, which runs hot under load.
mistakes.prevent: Blow through each jet and look for a clear passage.

steps.title: Install pistons with arrows forward
steps.action: Fit each piston with its graded rod shell, arrow toward the front, and tap it into the bore through a ring compressor while guiding the rod onto the journal.
steps.mistake: Installing a piston with its crown arrow facing the transmission end.

mistakes.title: Piston arrow facing the transmission
mistakes.what: Fitting a piston with its crown arrow pointing to the rear of the engine.
mistakes.consequence: The piston runs the wrong way round in its bore, which can cause noise and early wear and means a teardown to correct.
mistakes.prevent: Read the arrow on each crown before the piston goes into the ring compressor.

mistakes.title: Ring compressor not flat on the deck
mistakes.what: Holding the ring compressor at an angle or leaving it loose.
mistakes.consequence: A ring escapes between compressor and bore and breaks or catches.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten the compressor evenly and keep it flat on the deck while tapping the piston in.

mistakes.title: Hammering a piston that hangs up
mistakes.what: Driving a piston in harder when it hangs up on the deck.
mistakes.consequence: The ring catches on the deck edge, and the ring or the piston's ring land cracks.
mistakes.prevent: Stop, pull the piston back out and refit the compressor.

mistakes.title: Rod scratching the journal or liner
mistakes.what: Letting the rod swing into the bore wall or drop onto the journal.
mistakes.consequence: The rod end scores the liner wall or nicks the crank journal on its way down.
mistakes.prevent: Guide the rod by hand onto the journal with the journal protected.

mistakes.title: Fitting pistons into dry bores
mistakes.what: Fitting pistons into bores with no oil on the walls or rings.
mistakes.consequence: Rings and skirts scuff on the first cranking turns.
mistakes.prevent: Lightly oil the bores and rings before fitting.

steps.title: Fit and torque rod caps
steps.action: Mate each fracture-split cap to its own rod, then tighten the rod bolts to the JLR value and angle, using new bolts if the manual specifies them.
steps.why: A fracture-split cap only seats correctly on the rod it was broken from.
steps.mistake: Swapping caps between rods.

mistakes.title: Rod caps swapped between rods
mistakes.what: Fitting a rod cap to a rod it was not fracture-split from.
mistakes.consequence: The split faces cannot interlock, the big-end bore is out of shape and the bearing fails.
mistakes.prevent: Match each cap to its rod by the pairing marks and keep every pair together from teardown on.

mistakes.title: Rod cap fitted reversed
mistakes.what: Fitting a fracture-split cap turned 180 degrees.
mistakes.consequence: The fracture faces do not mate, the bore is wrong and the bearing fails.
mistakes.prevent: Match the cap to its rod by marks and feel the fracture faces lock together before tightening.

mistakes.title: Dirt or oil on fracture faces
mistakes.what: Wiping the cap's fracture faces with a rag or leaving oil on them.
mistakes.consequence: Lint or oil between the faces stops the cap from seating precisely.
mistakes.prevent: Clean the fracture faces with brake cleaner, blow them dry, and do not wipe them.

mistakes.title: Reusing the rod bolts
mistakes.what: Refitting the rod bolts removed at teardown.
mistakes.consequence: A fatigued or stretched bolt can fail and the rod lets go.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new rod bolts unless the JLR manual says otherwise.

mistakes.title: Using an unverified rod bolt torque
mistakes.what: Using a rod bolt torque from a forum or another engine.
mistakes.consequence: A wrong clamp load lets the cap move or overstretches the bolt.
mistakes.prevent: Look up the rod bolt torque and angle for this engine in TOPIx before starting the bottom end.

steps.title: Install the windage tray
steps.action: Bolt the structural windage tray to the bottom of the block.

steps.title: Install oil pump and pickup
steps.action: Fit the inlet pipe to the pump, bolt the pump to the block, then tighten the pickup support bolt and reconnect the pump solenoid.

spec.note: 4 oil pump bolts; inlet pipe and pickup bolts 12 N·m

mistakes.title: Reusing the pickup pipe seal
mistakes.what: Refitting the inlet pipe to the pump on its old seal.
mistakes.consequence: The pump draws air, aerating the oil and lowering pressure to the bearings, phasers and CVVL unit.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new seal to the inlet pipe and torque its bolts to specification.

steps.title: Fit the oil pump drive chain
steps.action: Fit the chain and sprocket with the sprocket correctly keyed to the pump shaft, hold the sprocket with the flange holding tool and fit a new bolt.

spec.note: new bolt, then plus 90 degrees

mistakes.title: Reusing the oil pump sprocket bolt
mistakes.what: Refitting the old oil pump sprocket bolt.
mistakes.consequence: The sprocket can work loose, the pump stops, and the engine loses oil pressure.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new bolt and tighten it to torque plus angle.

mistakes.title: Sprocket not keyed to the pump shaft
mistakes.what: Fitting the sprocket off its key or flat.
mistakes.consequence: The sprocket slips on the shaft and oil pressure drops or disappears.
mistakes.prevent: Check that the sprocket is fully seated on its key before fitting the bolt.

steps.title: Seal and fit the oil pan
steps.action: Lay a steady 3 mm bead of JLR-spec silicone, fit the pan and all bolts finger tight, then tighten in sequence in two stages, all within 7 minutes of laying the sealant.

spec.note: stage 1 10 N·m, stage 2 25 N·m, in sequence; fit within 7 minutes of laying the sealant

steps.mistake: Letting the RTV skin over before the pan is torqued.

mistakes.title: Letting the pan RTV skin over
mistakes.what: Fitting or tightening the pan after the sealant has begun to skin.
mistakes.consequence: The skinned bead does not wet both faces, so the pan leaks and has to come off again.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the pan and finish both tightening stages within 7 minutes of laying the bead.

mistakes.title: Laying too big an RTV bead
mistakes.what: Laying a heavy bead of sealant on the pan flange.
mistakes.consequence: The excess squeezes inside, breaks off and blocks the oil pickup screen, starving the bearings.
mistakes.prevent: Lay a steady bead of the specified size and wipe any inside squeeze-out you can reach.

mistakes.title: Pan bolts tightened out of order
mistakes.what: Tightening the pan bolts at random or in one stage.
mistakes.consequence: The pan is pulled down unevenly, the RTV is squeezed thin in places and the joint weeps.
mistakes.prevent: Fit all bolts finger tight, then tighten in sequence in both stages.

steps.title: Fit the engine front cover
steps.action: Apply RTV where shown, fit the front cover, align it with the JLR tool, and tighten four bolts in sequence and the remaining eight diagonally.

spec.note: all 12 bolts

mistakes.title: Front cover fitted without the alignment tool
mistakes.what: Bolting the front cover on by eye without the JLR alignment tool.
mistakes.consequence: The seal bore is off center on the crank and the front seal leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Use the alignment tool before tightening the cover bolts.

mistakes.title: Excess RTV on the front cover
mistakes.what: Applying too much sealant to the front cover joint.
mistakes.consequence: Squeeze-out breaks loose inside and can reach the oil pickup.
mistakes.prevent: Apply sealant only where shown and in the specified size.

steps.title: Install the front crank seal
steps.action: Install a new front seal dry with the JLR seal tool and turn it home to the specified torque.
steps.why: The seal goes on dry; it seals against the pulley hub.
steps.mistake: Oiling the new front seal.

mistakes.title: Oiling the front crank seal
mistakes.what: Lubricating the new front seal before fitting it.
mistakes.consequence: The front seal is meant to go on dry against the pulley hub, and oil on it can let the seal creep or weep.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the front seal clean and dry with the JLR seal tool.

mistakes.title: Front seal driven in crooked
mistakes.what: Starting the new seal at an angle on the tool.
mistakes.consequence: The seal lip runs off center on the pulley hub and leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Start the seal square on the tool and turn it home evenly.

steps.title: Fit the crankshaft pulley
steps.action: Fit the pulley onto its roll pin with a good O-ring, check that the four new bolts are 48 mm long, and tighten them diagonally.
steps.why: The pulley carries the timing mark and the locking tool needed for the timing steps.

spec.note: new 48 mm bolts, diagonal sequence, then plus 90 degrees

mistakes.title: Fitting wrong-length pulley bolts
mistakes.what: Fitting bolts of the wrong length to the pulley.
mistakes.consequence: A long bolt bottoms before clamping and a short one has too little thread, so the pulley can loosen.
mistakes.prevent: Check that each new bolt is 48 mm long before fitting.

mistakes.title: Skipping the pulley bolt angle
mistakes.what: Torquing the pulley bolts but not turning them the extra angle.
mistakes.consequence: Without the angle stage the pulley is under-clamped on the crank nose and can work loose.
mistakes.prevent: Apply the torque and then the angle, in the diagonal sequence.

mistakes.title: Fitting the pulley without its O-ring
mistakes.what: Fitting the pulley with a missing or damaged O-ring.
mistakes.consequence: Oil seeps out between the pulley and the crank nose and is flung around the front of the engine.
mistakes.prevent: Check that the O-ring is present and undamaged before fitting.

steps.title: Rebuild the valve assemblies
steps.action: Fit new stem seals, oil each valve stem, insert the valves in their original guides and refit springs, retainers and collets with the compressor.

mistakes.title: Cutting new stem seals on the collet grooves
mistakes.what: Pushing stem seals over the valve tips without protecting the seal lip.
mistakes.consequence: The sharp collet grooves cut the lip and the engine burns oil.
mistakes.prevent: Cover the valve tip while fitting each seal and push it on squarely.

mistakes.title: Collets not fully seated
mistakes.what: Leaving a collet half out of its groove after releasing the compressor.
mistakes.consequence: The retainer lets go, the valve drops into the cylinder and the engine is wrecked.
mistakes.prevent: Check that each pair of collets is seated and tap each valve tip lightly with a soft mallet to confirm.

mistakes.title: Valves swapped between guides
mistakes.what: Refitting valves to guides other than the ones they were lapped to.
mistakes.consequence: Seat contact is lost and the valve leaks compression.
mistakes.prevent: Work from the numbered rack, one valve at a time.

steps.title: Fit dowels and head gasket
steps.action: Fit the two clean dowels to the block and lay a new multi-layer steel gasket over them.
steps.mistake: Fitting the gasket without the dowels in place.

mistakes.title: Laying the gasket before the dowels
mistakes.what: Placing the new gasket on the block before fitting the dowels.
mistakes.consequence: The gasket can shift as the head comes down, partly covering passages or sitting over a bore edge.
mistakes.prevent: Fit both dowels first and drop the gasket over them.

mistakes.title: Fitting the head gasket upside down
mistakes.what: Laying the gasket on without checking its orientation marks.
mistakes.consequence: Coolant and oil holes do not line up, causing overheating or oil starvation to the head.
mistakes.prevent: Check that the gasket markings face as specified and that every hole lines up.

mistakes.title: Contaminating the gasket faces
mistakes.what: Touching the gasket or deck with oily hands, or letting dust settle before the head goes on.
mistakes.consequence: Contamination under the MLS gasket stops it from sealing.
mistakes.prevent: Wipe the deck dry and clean immediately before fitting the gasket and handle it by its edges.

steps.title: Set the head on its dowels
steps.action: With a helper, lower the head straight onto the dowels.

mistakes.title: Sliding the head across the gasket
mistakes.what: Setting the head down and sliding it into place on the dowels.
mistakes.consequence: The gasket coating is scraped or the gasket moves out of position.
mistakes.prevent: Lower the head straight down onto the dowels with a helper.

steps.title: Snug the new head bolts
steps.action: Fit ten new head bolts into clean, dry holes and tighten them in sequence with the JLR head bolt tool.
steps.why: These are torque-to-yield bolts, and oil in the blind holes gives false readings or can crack the block.

spec.note: new bolts, dry threads, in sequence

steps.mistake: Reusing the old stretched head bolts.

mistakes.title: Reusing the stretched head bolts
mistakes.what: Refitting the old head bolts, which were tightened past yield.
mistakes.consequence: A yielded bolt cannot reach the designed clamp load again, so the head gasket can fail in service.
mistakes.prevent: Fit ten new head bolts every time the head comes off.

mistakes.title: Leaving oil in the head bolt holes
mistakes.what: Leaving oil or water in the blind head bolt holes.
mistakes.consequence: The bolt cannot seat, torque reads falsely, and the block can crack.
mistakes.prevent: Blow every hole dry immediately before fitting the bolts.

mistakes.title: Oiling head bolts meant to go in dry
mistakes.what: Oiling the new head bolts although they are to be fitted dry.
mistakes.consequence: Oiled threads turn more of the torque into stretch, so the head bolts are over-clamped and can yield too far.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the bolts dry, as the head procedure requires.

mistakes.title: Leaving dirt in head bolt threads
mistakes.what: Leaving old sealant or debris in the block threads.
mistakes.consequence: Torque is used up on friction and the head is under-clamped, so the gasket leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Chase and clean every thread before assembly.

steps.title: Angle the head bolts
steps.action: In the same sequence, turn every head bolt 90 degrees, then a further 180 degrees.

spec.note: stage 1; then stage 2 a further 180 degrees, in sequence

steps.mistake: Stopping after the first angle stage or skipping the sequence.

mistakes.title: Stopping after the first angle stage
mistakes.what: Giving the head bolts their 90-degree turn but not the further 180 degrees, or angling them out of sequence.
mistakes.consequence: The head ends up badly under-clamped or clamped unevenly, and the gasket fails.
mistakes.prevent: Tick off every bolt at every stage on a printed sequence diagram.

mistakes.title: Guessing the angle stages
mistakes.what: Judging the 90- and 180-degree turns by eye.
mistakes.consequence: Clamp load varies from bolt to bolt and the gasket seals unevenly.
mistakes.prevent: Use an angle gauge or mark each bolt head and the head surface.

steps.title: Tighten the small head bolts
steps.action: Fit and tighten the single bolt, then the three small bolts at the timing end.

spec.note: single bolt; the three small bolts 12 N·m

mistakes.title: Forgetting the small head bolts
mistakes.what: Leaving out the three small bolts and the single bolt at the timing end.
mistakes.consequence: The timing end of the head is not clamped and leaks oil or coolant.
mistakes.prevent: Fit and torque the small bolts straight after the main bolts.

steps.title: Refit lash adjusters and followers
steps.action: Oil and refit the eight lash adjusters and eight roller followers in their original positions.

mistakes.title: Followers not seated on adjusters
mistakes.what: Leaving a roller follower only partly engaged on its lash adjuster and valve tip.
mistakes.consequence: The follower falls out when the cam is fitted or the engine is turned, bending a valve or breaking the follower.
mistakes.prevent: Check that each follower sits correctly on its adjuster and valve before fitting the cams.

steps.title: Install camshafts in the carrier
steps.action: Oil the needle bearings, lay each camshaft in the carrier, fit its five matched caps and tighten the bolts in sequence.

spec.note: cam cap bolts, in sequence

steps.mistake: Mixing up the I and E caps or their numbered positions.

mistakes.title: Refitting cam caps in the wrong places
mistakes.what: Refitting cam caps in the wrong place, or swapping an I cap with an E cap.
mistakes.consequence: A cap on the wrong bore binds the camshaft when tightened and wears its bearing quickly.
mistakes.prevent: Match every cap by its I or E stamp and number before fitting its bolts.

mistakes.title: Pulling cam caps down unevenly
mistakes.what: Tightening one cap fully while the others are loose.
mistakes.consequence: The cam is bent or cracked by uneven valve and pump spring force.
mistakes.prevent: Draw the caps down evenly a little at a time in sequence.

mistakes.title: Fitting cams onto dry bearings
mistakes.what: Laying the camshafts in without oiling the needle bearings.
mistakes.consequence: The cam needle rollers skid on dry races until the priming routine gets oil up to the carrier.
mistakes.prevent: Oil each needle bearing before laying in the cam.

steps.title: Fit the camshaft carrier
steps.action: Lay a new gasket on the head, set the carrier on its two dowels, and tighten the nineteen bolts in sequence in two stages.

spec.note: stage 1 10 N·m, stage 2 28 N·m, in sequence

mistakes.title: Skipping the first torque stage
mistakes.what: Tightening the carrier bolts straight to final torque.
mistakes.consequence: The carrier distorts and the cams may bind or the gasket leak.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten in sequence to the first stage, then to the final torque.

mistakes.title: Lowering the carrier off its dowels
mistakes.what: Lowering the carrier with a dowel missing or out of place.
mistakes.consequence: The carrier sits offset, the cams bind and the joint leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Check that both dowels are fitted and that the carrier drops onto them freely.

steps.title: Fit the camshaft sensors
steps.action: Install both camshaft position sensors with new O-rings.

mistakes.title: Reusing cam sensor O-rings
mistakes.what: Refitting the camshaft position sensors on their old O-rings.
mistakes.consequence: Hardened O-rings let oil weep from both cam sensors onto the carrier.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new O-ring to each sensor and push the sensor in straight.

mistakes.title: Overtightening the cam sensors
mistakes.what: Tightening the cam sensor bolts beyond their low specified torque.
mistakes.consequence: The sensor flange cracks or the carrier thread strips.
mistakes.prevent: Use a small torque wrench set to the sensors' 8 N·m figure.

steps.title: Set the crank to timing position
steps.action: Turn the crank clockwise with the rotation tool until the pulley mark points down, then fit and bolt the crank pulley locking tool.

spec.note: after TDC, cylinder 1

steps.mistake: Rotating the crank counter-clockwise.

mistakes.title: Turning the crank counter-clockwise
mistakes.what: Turning the crank backward to reach the timing position during assembly.
mistakes.consequence: Reverse rotation can bring a piston up against a valve held open by a cam, or slacken a chain that is fitted.
mistakes.prevent: Turn clockwise only, and go around again if you overshoot the mark.

mistakes.title: Setting the cams before the crank
mistakes.what: Locking the cams in their timing position before turning the crank to 50 degrees after TDC.
mistakes.consequence: Turning the crank through TDC with valves open on a cam can drive a piston into a valve.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the crank to its position and lock it first, then turn the cams.

mistakes.title: Fitting the pulley lock without locking it
mistakes.what: Fitting the pulley locking tool but not locking it.
mistakes.consequence: The crank moves while the chains are fitted, putting the timing off.
mistakes.prevent: Lock the tool and check that the crank will not move before fitting the chains.

steps.title: Lock the cams with the setting tool
steps.action: Turn each camshaft until its mark points up and bolt the camshaft setting tool across both.

spec.note: tool bolts

mistakes.title: Setting a cam mark at 6 o'clock
mistakes.what: Turning a cam until its mark points down instead of up.
mistakes.consequence: The cam is 180 degrees out and the engine will not run correctly; forcing the tool on hides the error.
mistakes.prevent: Set both cam marks at 12 o'clock and fit the tool without force.

steps.title: Fit idler with primary chain
steps.action: Hang the new primary chain on the idler sprocket with the timing mark at the center of the gold link, fit the idler and chain together, and tighten the idler bolt.
steps.why: The colored links are the only reference for chain-to-sprocket timing.
steps.mistake: Letting the chain slip a tooth off its colored link while fitting the idler.

mistakes.title: Letting the chain slip off its colored link
mistakes.what: Letting the primary chain move a tooth off its colored link while fitting the idler and chain together.
mistakes.consequence: Cam timing ends up a tooth out, giving codes and poor running and risking valve contact.
mistakes.prevent: Hold the chain on the idler with the mark centered on the colored link and recheck before tightening the bolt.

mistakes.title: Leaving the idler bolt undertightened
mistakes.what: Snugging the idler sprocket bolt by feel because no torque value is on hand.
mistakes.consequence: The idler can work loose, letting both chains lose timing on an interference engine.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten the idler bolt to the value in the JLR manual.

mistakes.title: Timing an old chain without colored links
mistakes.what: Reusing the old chain, which has no colored links.
mistakes.consequence: With no reference marks on the chain, the timing ends up off.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the new chain with its colored links on the sprocket marks.

steps.title: Fit new primary chain guides
steps.action: Confirm the crank and idler marks still align, then fit the new fixed guide and the new tensioner guide.

spec.note: two-bolt guide; single-bolt guide 11 N·m

mistakes.title: Reusing the primary chain guides
mistakes.what: Refitting the old primary chain guides with the new primary chain.
mistakes.consequence: Grooved guides let the primary chain whip, wearing the new chain and the idler early.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new guides whenever the chain is replaced.

mistakes.title: Swapping guide bolt torques
mistakes.what: Torquing the two-bolt guide and the single-bolt guide to each other's values.
mistakes.consequence: The single-bolt guide is overtightened and strips, or the two-bolt guide is left loose.
mistakes.prevent: Check the torque for each guide before tightening.

steps.title: Fit the new primary tensioner
steps.action: Bolt on the new primary chain tensioner, then pull out and discard its locking clip.

mistakes.title: Forgetting to pull the tensioner clip
mistakes.what: Leaving the primary tensioner's locking clip in.
mistakes.consequence: The chain runs slack, rattles and can jump on an interference engine.
mistakes.prevent: Pull and discard the clip immediately after the tensioner is bolted down.
mistakes.detect: Chain slack you can feel or a rattle on first turn.

mistakes.title: Releasing the tensioner before bolting it
mistakes.what: Pulling the clip before the tensioner is bolted down.
mistakes.consequence: The plunger extends and the tensioner will not fit without resetting.
mistakes.prevent: Bolt the tensioner down first, then pull the clip.

steps.title: Hang the secondary chain
steps.action: Fit the new secondary chain over the idler with its colored link on the idler mark, keeping tension on the chain so it cannot jump.

mistakes.title: Leaving slack in the secondary chain
mistakes.what: Fitting the secondary chain with slack between the idler and the intake sprocket.
mistakes.consequence: The chain ends up a tooth off once tension is applied.
mistakes.prevent: Keep the chain taut on the drive side as each sprocket and guide goes on.

steps.title: Fit the first secondary guide
steps.action: Install the first new secondary chain guide while keeping the chain taut.

steps.title: Fit the intake phaser
steps.action: Fit the intake VCT actuator on its dowel with the colored link centered on its mark, then snug a new center bolt and back it off a quarter turn.
steps.why: Backing the bolt off leaves the sprocket free to settle under chain tension before final torque.

spec.note: new bolt, then loosen 90 degrees

steps.mistake: Fitting the phaser off its dowel or fitting the exhaust phaser to the intake cam.

mistakes.title: Misfitting the intake phaser
mistakes.what: Fitting the intake phaser off its dowel, or putting the exhaust phaser on the intake cam.
mistakes.consequence: The intake cam runs mistimed or with the wrong phasing range and sets cam timing codes.
mistakes.prevent: Check the label and part number, and feel the phaser seat on its dowel before fitting the bolt.

mistakes.title: Skipping the back-off on the phaser bolt
mistakes.what: Leaving the intake phaser bolt snug instead of backing it off the specified quarter turn.
mistakes.consequence: The sprocket cannot settle under chain tension and the cam timing ends up off.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten to the first stage, then back off 90 degrees as specified.

steps.title: Fit the middle secondary guide
steps.action: Install the second new secondary chain guide between the camshaft sprockets, keeping the chain on the idler.

steps.title: Fit the exhaust phaser
steps.action: Fit the exhaust VCT actuator on its dowel with its groove centered on the colored link, then snug a new bolt and back it off a quarter turn.

spec.note: new bolt, then loosen 90 degrees

mistakes.title: Fitting the exhaust phaser off its dowel
mistakes.what: Fitting the exhaust phaser without its dowel engaging.
mistakes.consequence: The exhaust cam is mistimed, giving codes and poor running.
mistakes.prevent: Check that the dowel engages and that the timing marks line up before fitting the bolt.

steps.title: Fit the tensioner-side guide
steps.action: Install the last new secondary chain guide with its two bolts.

steps.title: Lock the phasers with the VCT tool
steps.action: Bolt the VCT actuator locking tool over both phasers.

spec.note: tool bolts

mistakes.title: Torquing phaser bolts without the VCT lock
mistakes.what: Giving the phaser bolts their final torque without the VCT locking tool fitted.
mistakes.consequence: The phasers turn under the wrench and the cam timing shifts.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the VCT locking tool before final torque.

steps.title: Install the new secondary tensioner
steps.action: Screw in the new, still-compressed hydraulic secondary (upper) tensioner.

mistakes.title: Fitting the tensioner uncompressed
mistakes.what: Screwing in the secondary tensioner while its plunger is extended.
mistakes.consequence: The tensioner does not fit correctly and loads the chain wrongly.
mistakes.prevent: Check that the tensioner is compressed before fitting it, as the bulletin requires.

mistakes.title: Reusing the old secondary tensioner
mistakes.what: Refitting the removed tensioner to save a part.
mistakes.consequence: A worn tensioner does not take up slack and the chain rattles.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new tensioner every time the old one comes out.

steps.title: Release the secondary tensioner
steps.action: Push the secondary tensioner guide in and let it go to release the tensioner plunger, without touching the tensioner itself, and confirm that the chain is now taut.
steps.mistake: Torquing the phaser bolts before the tensioner has released and taken up the slack.

mistakes.title: Torquing phaser bolts before tensioner release
mistakes.what: Tightening the phaser bolts fully while the secondary tensioner is still compressed.
mistakes.consequence: The sprockets are locked with slack in the chain, so the timing shifts once the tensioner extends.
mistakes.prevent: Release the tensioner and confirm the chain is taut before the final torque stage.

mistakes.title: Pressing on the tensioner directly
mistakes.what: Pushing on the tensioner body or plunger to release it.
mistakes.consequence: The tensioner is damaged or not released correctly.
mistakes.prevent: Release the tensioner by pushing on the guide only.

mistakes.title: Not checking that the plunger extended
mistakes.what: Assuming the tensioner has released without checking.
mistakes.consequence: A stuck plunger leaves the chain slack, and the chain can jump.
mistakes.prevent: Check that the plunger is fully extended and the chain is taut before final torque.

steps.title: Final-torque the phaser bolts
steps.action: With the locking tools still fitted, tighten both VCT center bolts to torque and then the final angle.

spec.note: then plus 60 degrees

steps.mistake: Reusing the old center bolts, which are single use.

mistakes.title: Reusing the VCT center bolts
mistakes.what: Refitting the old phaser center bolts.
mistakes.consequence: Single-use bolts that have already been angled cannot hold the clamp, so a phaser can slip on its cam.
mistakes.prevent: Use the new center bolts supplied with the phasers or timing kit, never the removed ones.

mistakes.title: Skipping the 60-degree angle
mistakes.what: Torquing the phaser bolts but not turning them the final angle.
mistakes.consequence: The phaser can slip on the cam, causing timing drift and codes.
mistakes.prevent: Apply the torque, then the full angle, using an angle gauge.

steps.title: Remove the cam locking tools
steps.action: Remove the VCT locking tool, then the camshaft setting tool.

mistakes.title: Turning the crank with tools fitted
mistakes.what: Turning the crank while the camshaft setting tool or VCT lock is still bolted on.
mistakes.consequence: The tools fight the chain, which can bend a tool, twist a camshaft or jump the chain.
mistakes.prevent: Remove both cam tools and the crank lock before turning the engine.

steps.title: Verify timing after two turns
steps.action: Remove the crank lock, turn the engine clockwise two full turns by hand, and confirm the pulley and cam marks line up again and the setting tool still fits without force.
steps.why: The check catches a chain one tooth out before the covers go on and before the engine is fired.
steps.mistake: Closing up the timing covers without a hand-turn check.

mistakes.title: Closing up without a hand-turn check
mistakes.what: Fitting the covers straight after the timing tools come off.
mistakes.consequence: A chain a tooth out is only found at start-up, after the covers and drive plate are back on.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the engine two full turns by hand and recheck every mark before fitting the covers.

mistakes.title: Checking after only one turn
mistakes.what: Turning the crank one revolution and checking the marks.
mistakes.consequence: The cams line up only every second turn, so one turn proves nothing.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the crank two full turns clockwise before checking.

mistakes.title: Forcing the setting tool during the check
mistakes.what: Tapping the setting tool into place during the timing check.
mistakes.consequence: A one-tooth error is hidden and the engine is closed up mistimed.
mistakes.prevent: If the tool does not fit freely, find out why before closing up.

mistakes.title: Turning backwards to line up marks
mistakes.what: Turning the crank back when it goes past the marks.
mistakes.consequence: Backward rotation can let the chain go slack against the tensioner and jump.
mistakes.prevent: If the mark goes past, carry on clockwise for another two full turns.

steps.title: Seal the lower timing cover
steps.action: Lay a continuous 3 mm RTV bead, check the dowels, and fit the lower timing cover within 7 minutes, taking care not to damage the head gasket edge.
steps.why: The cover spans the head-to-block joint and closes the rear of the block.

spec.note: maximum time from laying the sealant to fitting

steps.mistake: Catching and tearing the exposed edge of the new head gasket with the cover.

mistakes.title: Tearing the head gasket edge
mistakes.what: Sliding the lower timing cover into place so it catches the exposed edge of the new head gasket.
mistakes.consequence: The torn gasket edge leaks oil or coolant at the rear of the engine.
mistakes.prevent: Offer the cover straight onto its dowels, watching the gasket edge as it goes on.

mistakes.title: Fitting the cover after the RTV skins
mistakes.what: Fitting the lower timing cover after the RTV has started to skin over.
mistakes.consequence: The cover joint leaks at the back of the engine, and fixing it means pulling the transmission and drive plate again.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the cover within 7 minutes of laying the bead, and clean off and re-lay sealant if you miss it.

mistakes.title: Laying a broken or heavy RTV bead
mistakes.what: Laying a bead on the lower cover with gaps in it, or much heavier than specified.
mistakes.consequence: Gaps leak oil at the rear of the engine, and excess squeezed inside can break off and reach the oil pickup.
mistakes.prevent: Lay one continuous bead of the specified size around the whole flange.

steps.title: Torque the lower cover in stages
steps.action: Snug the two locating bolts, add two more and tighten all four, then fit and tighten the remaining twelve by size.

spec.note: first 2 bolts 5 N·m; then 4 bolts and M8 bolts 25 N·m; M6 bolts 12 N·m

mistakes.title: Tightening lower cover bolts out of order
mistakes.what: Running the lower timing cover bolts down in any order without first snugging the two locating bolts.
mistakes.consequence: The cover is drawn off its dowels and the RTV joint is squeezed unevenly, so it leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Snug the two locating bolts first, then the next four, then the remaining twelve by size.

mistakes.title: Torquing M6 cover bolts as M8
mistakes.what: Tightening the small M6 cover bolts to the higher M8 figure.
mistakes.consequence: The M6 bolts stretch or strip their threads in the aluminum cover or block.
mistakes.prevent: Sort the bolts by size before starting and use the M6 value on the M6 bolts.

steps.title: Refit the crank position sensor
steps.action: Fit the crankshaft position sensor to the lower timing cover, where it reads the drive plate reluctor ring.

mistakes.title: Bolting down a cocked crank sensor
mistakes.what: Bolting down the crankshaft position sensor while it is cocked in its bore.
mistakes.consequence: The gap to the drive plate reluctor is wrong, giving a weak signal, misfire codes or a no-start.
mistakes.prevent: Seat the sensor fully by hand before torquing its bolt to specification.

mistakes.title: Leaving swarf on the crank sensor tip
mistakes.what: Refitting the sensor with metal particles still clinging to its tip.
mistakes.consequence: Debris on the tip distorts the reluctor signal and can cause intermittent crank position faults.
mistakes.prevent: Wipe the sensor tip clean and check it for damage before fitting.

steps.title: Install the rear crank seal
steps.action: Fit the JLR installer to the crank, slide the new seal over it on its shipping spacer, discard the spacer, then draw the seal home until the tool bolt stops.
steps.why: The spacer keeps the seal lip correctly formed; a seal that slips off it must be replaced.
steps.mistake: Pushing the seal over the crank flange without its spacer and rolling the lip.

mistakes.title: Pushing the seal on without its spacer
mistakes.what: Pushing the new rear seal over the crank flange without its shipping spacer.
mistakes.consequence: The lip rolls over as it passes the flange and the seal leaks straight away.
mistakes.prevent: Slide the seal on with its spacer over the JLR installer and draw it home with the tool.

mistakes.title: Refitting a seal that left its spacer
mistakes.what: Pushing a rear seal that slipped off its shipping spacer back on and fitting it anyway.
mistakes.consequence: Once off the spacer the lip loses its formed shape, and the seal leaks soon after.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new seal if it ever comes off its spacer before installation.

mistakes.title: Not drawing the rear seal fully home
mistakes.what: Stopping before the installer bolt reaches its stop.
mistakes.consequence: The seal sits proud at the wrong depth and its lip runs on the wrong part of the flange.
mistakes.prevent: Draw the seal in until the tool bolt stops, then check that it sits square.

steps.title: Install the drive plate
steps.action: Fit the drive plate on its dowel with eight new bolts into clean, dry threads, then tighten in sequence with the crank locked.

spec.note: new pre-coated bolts, then plus 120 degrees, in sequence

steps.mistake: Reusing the drive plate bolts, which carry a one-time sealant patch.

mistakes.title: Reusing the drive plate bolts
mistakes.what: Refitting the old drive plate bolts.
mistakes.consequence: The old bolts' one-time thread patch and stretch are used up, so they can loosen or let oil past.
mistakes.prevent: Fit eight new pre-coated bolts and never reuse the old ones.

mistakes.title: Leaving oil in the drive plate holes
mistakes.what: Leaving oil or old thread patch material in the drive plate bolt holes.
mistakes.consequence: The new bolts' pre-applied patch cannot grip, and torque plus angle no longer gives the right clamp.
mistakes.prevent: Clean and dry each hole, chasing it no deeper than the depth limit if needed.

mistakes.title: Bolting the drive plate off its dowel
mistakes.what: Bolting on the drive plate without engaging its locating dowel.
mistakes.consequence: The plate runs out of true, the reluctor ring reads wrongly and the torque converter can vibrate.
mistakes.prevent: Engage the dowel and check that the plate sits flat before fitting any bolt.

mistakes.title: Skipping the drive plate angle stage
mistakes.what: Torquing the drive plate bolts but leaving off the 120-degree stage.
mistakes.consequence: The plate is under-clamped on the crank flange and can work loose behind the transmission.
mistakes.prevent: Apply the torque and then the full angle in sequence, marking each bolt as it is done.

steps.title: Fit the upper timing cover
steps.action: Apply a 3 mm sealant bead where shown, fit a new gasket and the cover, then tighten, back off and retighten every bolt.

spec.note: stage 1 13.5 N·m, stage 2 loosen 180 degrees, stage 3 13.5 N·m

mistakes.title: Skipping the loosen-and-retighten stage
mistakes.what: Tightening the upper cover bolts once instead of tightening, loosening 180 degrees and retightening them.
mistakes.consequence: The new gasket does not settle evenly and the upper cover weeps oil.
mistakes.prevent: Run all three stages in the specified pattern on every bolt.

steps.title: Refit the VCT solenoids
steps.action: Oil the bores, fit new O-rings and install both VCT solenoids into the upper timing cover.
steps.mistake: Fitting old O-rings; a leaking solenoid seal drops phaser oil pressure.

mistakes.title: Refitting old solenoid O-rings
mistakes.what: Refitting the VCT solenoids on their old O-rings.
mistakes.consequence: A leaking O-ring lowers oil pressure to the phaser and causes cam timing codes.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new O-rings to both VCT solenoids every time they come out.

mistakes.title: Pushing solenoids into dry bores
mistakes.what: Pushing the VCT solenoids into their bores without oiling them.
mistakes.consequence: The O-ring is sliced on the bore edge as it goes in, and the damage stays hidden until it leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Oil the bores and O-rings and push each solenoid in straight.

mistakes.title: Refitting superseded VCT solenoids
mistakes.what: Refitting the original VCT solenoids on an engine covered by service action N481.
mistakes.consequence: The flat spots, induction noise and VCT codes the service action fixes can come back.
mistakes.prevent: Check the VIN against N481 and fit the current solenoids if it applies.

steps.title: Reset the CVVL brake units
steps.action: If the original CVVL unit is going back on, reset all eight brake units with the JLR reset tool, keeping the unit upright.
steps.why: The brake units also act as the intake valve lash adjusters and must start from the reset position.
steps.mistake: Refitting a removed CVVL unit without resetting its brake units.

mistakes.title: Skipping the brake unit reset
mistakes.what: Refitting a removed CVVL unit without resetting its brake units.
mistakes.consequence: The brake units do not start from their reset position, so intake valve lash is wrong and the engine misfires.
mistakes.prevent: Reset all eight brake units with JLR-303-1639 before the unit goes back on.

steps.title: Install the CVVL unit
steps.action: With a new gasket and the locating pins fitted, lower the CVVL unit on and draw down the two pilot bolts in the specified way.

spec.note: 2 pilot bolts: run to contact, then 2 more turns, then 6 N·m

mistakes.title: Ignoring the pilot bolt method
mistakes.what: Pulling the CVVL unit down on all its bolts at once instead of on the two pilot bolts first.
mistakes.consequence: The unit is drawn onto its locating pins unevenly and can bind or be damaged as it seats.
mistakes.prevent: Run the two pilot bolts to contact, then two more turns, then to 6 N·m, before fitting the rest.

mistakes.title: Reusing the CVVL gasket
mistakes.what: Refitting the old CVVL gasket to avoid waiting for parts.
mistakes.consequence: Oil leaks from the CVVL joint onto the head and the unit has to come off again.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new CVVL gasket every time the unit is removed.

mistakes.title: Fitting injectors before the CVVL
mistakes.what: Fitting the injectors back into the head before the CVVL unit is refitted.
mistakes.consequence: The CVVL unit then has to be lowered past the fitted injectors, risking damage to both.
mistakes.prevent: Fit and torque the CVVL unit first, then the injectors.

steps.title: Torque the CVVL bolts
steps.action: Remove the locating pins, fit the last two bolts, and tighten all ten CVVL bolts in sequence.

spec.note: 10 bolts, in sequence

mistakes.title: Tightening CVVL bolts out of sequence
mistakes.what: Tightening the ten CVVL bolts in a random order.
mistakes.consequence: The unit is pulled down unevenly onto its gasket, which can leak or strain the housing.
mistakes.prevent: Remove the pins, fit the last two bolts and tighten all ten in the specified sequence.

steps.title: Fit the vent oil separator
steps.action: Fit the engine vent oil separator with a new gasket and tighten its seven bolts in sequence.

mistakes.title: Reusing the separator gasket
mistakes.what: Refitting the vent oil separator on its old gasket.
mistakes.consequence: The crankcase ventilation leaks, giving oil weeps or unmetered air and an uneven idle.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new separator gasket; the old one has taken a set.

steps.title: Fit the oil filter housing
steps.action: Fit five new O-rings, bolt the filter housing on, check the bypass valve in the cap, and fit a new element and cap O-ring.

spec.note: filter cap; housing bolts 11.5 N·m

steps.mistake: Fitting the filter cap without checking that the bypass valve is clipped in.

mistakes.title: Filter bypass valve not clipped in
mistakes.what: Fitting the filter cap without checking that the bypass valve is clipped into it.
mistakes.consequence: A loose bypass valve can let oil skip the filter element or drop into the housing.
mistakes.prevent: Check that the bypass valve is clipped firmly in the cap before fitting it.

mistakes.title: Reusing filter housing O-rings
mistakes.what: Reusing the five filter housing O-rings.
mistakes.consequence: Pressurized oil leaks from the housing joint and the oil level falls between checks.
mistakes.prevent: Fit all five new O-rings, lightly oiled, before bolting the housing on.

mistakes.title: Overtightening the filter cap
mistakes.what: Cranking the filter cap down hard to stop a leak.
mistakes.consequence: The cap or the housing thread is damaged and has to be replaced.
mistakes.prevent: Hand-tighten the cap on a new O-ring, then finish with a torque wrench set to the cap value.

steps.title: Fit new temperature sensors
steps.action: Install a new cylinder head temperature sensor with its special socket and a new block temperature sensor.

mistakes.title: Fitting the head temp sensor without its socket
mistakes.what: Fitting the cylinder head temperature sensor with an ordinary deep socket.
mistakes.consequence: The sensor body is damaged and its temperature reading can no longer be trusted.
mistakes.prevent: Use the special socket the procedure calls for and fit a new sensor.

steps.title: Refit the knock sensors
steps.action: Install both knock sensors on clean faces in their noted positions.

mistakes.title: Torquing a knock sensor by feel
mistakes.what: Tightening a knock sensor by feel instead of with a torque wrench.
mistakes.consequence: Sensor output depends on how firmly it is clamped, so the PCM may pull timing needlessly or miss real knock.
mistakes.prevent: Torque each sensor to its 20 N·m specification.

mistakes.title: Leaving dirt under a knock sensor
mistakes.what: Fitting the sensor on a face with paint, rust or old sealant on it.
mistakes.consequence: The sensor is coupled poorly to the block and picks up knock only weakly.
mistakes.prevent: Clean the mounting face to bare metal before fitting the sensor in its noted position.

steps.title: Refit block solenoid and connector
steps.action: Install the piston cooling jet solenoid and the vacuum pipe connector with oiled O-rings.

spec.note: piston cooling jet solenoid; vacuum connector 5 N·m

mistakes.title: Fitting the jet solenoid on dry O-rings
mistakes.what: Pushing in the piston cooling jet solenoid with dry O-rings.
mistakes.consequence: The O-rings roll or tear and the solenoid joint leaks oil.
mistakes.prevent: Smear clean oil on both O-rings and seat the solenoid by hand before torquing it.

steps.title: Size new injector seals
steps.action: Fit a new O-ring and washer, push a new Teflon seal on with the installer, wait two minutes, then form it with the resizing tool and fit a new spring clamp.
steps.why: An unsized Teflon seal will not enter the bore cleanly or seal combustion pressure. JLR warns that the Bosch sheet in the refit kit gives the steps in the wrong order.
steps.mistake: Following the Bosch sheet in the injector refit kit, whose wrong step order damages the seals and causes fuel leaks.

mistakes.title: Following the Bosch kit sheet
mistakes.what: Fitting the injector seals by the Bosch instruction sheet packed in the JLR refit kit.
mistakes.consequence: JLR found that sheet lists the steps in the wrong order, which damages the seals and causes fuel leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Set the Bosch sheet aside and follow the JLR injector procedure.

mistakes.title: Lubricating the Teflon seal
mistakes.what: Oiling or greasing the new Teflon seal to help it slide on.
mistakes.consequence: Lubricant on a Teflon combustion seal goes against the seal maker's instructions and can stop it from sealing.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the seal clean and dry with the installer, handling it as little as possible.

mistakes.title: Skipping the wait or the resizing
mistakes.what: Fitting the injector straight after pushing the seal on, without the two-minute wait and the resizing tool.
mistakes.consequence: The stretched seal is still oversize and is shaved or rolled as it enters the bore.
mistakes.prevent: Wait the two minutes and form the seal with the resizing tool before fitting.

mistakes.title: Nicking the Teflon seal
mistakes.what: Pushing the seal on with fingernails or a screwdriver.
mistakes.consequence: A small cut in the Teflon seal lets combustion gas past the injector.
mistakes.prevent: Use the installer cone and gentle finger pressure only.

mistakes.title: Leaving a sized injector waiting too long
mistakes.what: Sizing the injectors and then leaving them on the bench while other work is done.
mistakes.consequence: The Teflon seal starts to expand again and will not enter the bore cleanly.
mistakes.prevent: Size each seal just before that injector goes into the head.

steps.title: Install injectors and rail
steps.action: Clip the injectors to the rail, guide the assembly in on the JLR guide pins, and tighten the rail bolts one turn at a time.
tools: JLR-310-255 (original head) or JLR-310-256 (new head) guide pins

spec.note: rail bolts one turn at a time; final 4 bolts 30 N·m in sequence

steps.mistake: Pulling the rail down on one bolt and cocking an injector in its bore.

mistakes.title: Pulling the rail down on one bolt
mistakes.what: Drawing the fuel rail down by one bolt at a time.
mistakes.consequence: An injector cocks in its bore and its new seal is damaged.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten the rail bolts one turn at a time, alternating, to torque.

mistakes.title: Fitting the rail without guide pins
mistakes.what: Lowering the rail and injectors into place without the JLR guide pins.
mistakes.consequence: Injectors can be pushed in off-center and the rail-to-injector joints may not seat, so fuel leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the JLR guide pins and lower the rail and injectors together along them.

mistakes.title: Getting lint in the injector inlets
mistakes.what: Touching the rail and injector inlets with rags, lint or dirty fingers during assembly.
mistakes.consequence: One fiber caught at an injector inlet can upset its spray and cause a misfire on that cylinder.
mistakes.prevent: Work with lint-free cloths and keep caps on every opening until the moment it is connected.

mistakes.title: Reusing the injector clamps
mistakes.what: Refitting the old injector spring clamps.
mistakes.consequence: A tired clamp does not hold the injector down firmly, so the injector can move and wear its seal.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new spring clamps from the refit kit.

steps.title: Fit coils and spark plugs
steps.action: Install the spark plugs, then the four ignition coils.

spec.note: coil bolts

mistakes.title: Cross-threading a spark plug
mistakes.what: Starting a plug in the aluminum head with a ratchet.
mistakes.consequence: The thread in the head is damaged and needs a thread repair insert.
mistakes.prevent: Start every plug by hand for several turns, in a clean plug hole, before using a wrench.

mistakes.title: Torquing spark plugs by feel
mistakes.what: Tightening plugs by feel rather than with a torque wrench.
mistakes.consequence: A loose plug runs hot and can cause pre-ignition, while an overtightened one stretches its shell or cracks the insulator.
mistakes.prevent: Torque each plug to the maker's figure for an aluminum head, on a cool engine.

steps.title: Install the HP fuel pump
steps.action: Oil and fit the tappet, then draw the pump down evenly one turn per bolt, alternating, to torque.
steps.mistake: Pulling the pump down on one bolt against the cam lobe spring load.

mistakes.title: Pulling the HP fuel pump down on one bolt
mistakes.what: Tightening one pump bolt fully while the other is still loose.
mistakes.consequence: The cam lobe spring load cocks the pump and can crack its flange.
mistakes.prevent: Draw the pump down one turn per bolt, alternating, to torque.

mistakes.title: Fitting the pump tappet dry
mistakes.what: Fitting the HP fuel pump tappet into its bore without oil.
mistakes.consequence: The tappet and pump lobe scuff on first crank before oil reaches them.
mistakes.prevent: Oil the tappet and its bore and check that it slides freely before fitting the pump.

steps.title: Torque the HP fuel lines
steps.action: Fit the HP lines finger tight, tighten the unions in sequence, wait 30 seconds and recheck, then paint-mark each line.

spec.note: unions; recheck after 30 seconds

mistakes.title: Skipping the HP union recheck
mistakes.what: Tightening the HP unions once and not rechecking them after 30 seconds.
mistakes.consequence: A union that relaxes can leak fuel at direct-injection pressure, a fire risk on a hot engine.
mistakes.prevent: Wait 30 seconds after the first tightening and recheck every union to torque.

mistakes.title: Not paint-marking the HP line
mistakes.what: Fitting the line without adding a new paint mark.
mistakes.consequence: The next technician cannot count the tightening cycles and may reuse a line past its limit.
mistakes.prevent: Paint-mark each line once its unions are at final torque.

mistakes.title: Starting HP unions with a wrench
mistakes.what: Starting the HP unions with a wrench instead of by hand.
mistakes.consequence: A cross-threaded union never seals, and the line or the part it screws into must be replaced.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the lines finger tight at both ends before any tool touches them.

steps.title: Refit the thermostat housing
steps.action: Install the thermostat housing with an undamaged gasket.

steps.title: Install the intake manifold
steps.action: Fit four new port seals and the manifold, then tighten the seven bolts in sequence.

mistakes.title: Reusing intake port seals
mistakes.what: Reusing the four old intake port seals.
mistakes.consequence: Air leaks past the seals, causing lean fuel trim codes and an unsteady idle.
mistakes.prevent: Fit four new port seals each time the manifold comes off.

mistakes.title: Leaving debris in the intake tract
mistakes.what: Leaving tape, rags or dropped bolts in the ports or the manifold.
mistakes.consequence: Anything left in the intake is drawn into a cylinder on first start and can damage a valve or piston.
mistakes.prevent: Look into each port and the manifold with a light before fitting it.

steps.title: Install the oil cooler
steps.action: Fit a new metal gasket and the oil cooler, and tighten the seven bolts in sequence in two stages.

spec.note: stage 1 15 N·m, stage 2 25 N·m, in sequence

mistakes.title: Reusing the oil cooler gasket
mistakes.what: Refitting the old metal oil cooler gasket.
mistakes.consequence: Oil or coolant leaks from the cooler joint below the turbo.
mistakes.prevent: Use a new metal gasket; a crushed one cannot seal a second time.

steps.title: Mount the turbocharger
steps.action: Fit a new gasket and the turbo to the head, and tighten four new nuts in sequence in two stages.

spec.note: new nuts, stage 1 18 N·m, stage 2 25 N·m, in sequence

mistakes.title: Reusing the turbo nuts
mistakes.what: Refitting the old turbo nuts to the head.
mistakes.consequence: Heat-cycled nuts lose their grip, so the turbo flange leaks exhaust and the nuts back off.
mistakes.prevent: Fit four new nuts from the kit and torque them in two stages.

mistakes.title: Leaving blanking plugs in the turbo
mistakes.what: Leaving plastic or foam shipping plugs in a new turbo.
mistakes.consequence: A plug in an oil port starves the bearings, and one in the air path is swallowed by the wheels.
mistakes.prevent: Remove every plug and cap from the turbo before fitting it.

steps.title: Fit the turbo oil return
steps.action: Install the oil return pipe with two new O-rings.

mistakes.title: Reusing return pipe O-rings
mistakes.what: Reusing the two oil return O-rings.
mistakes.consequence: Oil weeps from the return joint onto the hot exhaust side.
mistakes.prevent: Fit two new O-rings to the return pipe, lightly oiled.

mistakes.title: Restricting the turbo oil return
mistakes.what: Fitting the return pipe kinked or with a blocked passage.
mistakes.consequence: Oil backs up in the bearing housing and is pushed past the turbo seals, causing smoke.
mistakes.prevent: Check that the return pipe is clear and runs downhill without kinks.

steps.title: Prime the turbo and fit its feed
steps.action: Fill the turbo oil inlet with clean engine oil, then fit the feed pipe with new banjo bolts and four new sealing washers, and refit its bracket.
steps.why: Pre-oiling the bearings protects them during the seconds before oil pressure reaches the turbo on first crank.

spec.note: new banjo bolts and washers

steps.mistake: Connecting a dry turbo and relying on the first crank to oil it.

mistakes.title: Connecting a dry turbo
mistakes.what: Connecting the turbo oil feed without filling the turbo inlet with oil.
mistakes.consequence: The bearings run dry for the seconds before oil pressure reaches them on first crank.
mistakes.prevent: Fill the turbo inlet with clean engine oil before fitting the feed pipe.

mistakes.title: Reusing banjo bolts or washers
mistakes.what: Refitting the old banjo bolts or sealing washers on the turbo feed.
mistakes.consequence: A reused washer does not crush again, and oil drips onto the hot turbo.
mistakes.prevent: Fit two new banjo bolts and four new washers.

mistakes.title: Reusing a doubtful oil feed pipe
mistakes.what: Putting the old feed pipe back on a new turbo without checking it.
mistakes.consequence: Carbon or debris inside the pipe is flushed straight into the new turbo's bearings.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new oil feed pipe whenever the turbo is replaced, as the turbo maker recommends.

mistakes.title: Not spinning the wheel after priming
mistakes.what: Skipping the hand turn of the compressor wheel after priming the turbo.
mistakes.consequence: A turbo that binds or rubs is not noticed until after start-up.
mistakes.prevent: Spin the wheel a few times after priming; it should turn freely.

steps.title: Refit the turbo heat shields
steps.action: Install the heat shields, using a new bolt where the procedure calls for one.

steps.title: Install the coolant pump
steps.action: Fit the coolant pump, tighten the two locating bolts first, then the other four, and fit the pulley.

spec.note: all 6 pump bolts, after the 2 locating bolts at 6 N·m; pulley bolts 25 N·m

mistakes.title: Tightening pump bolts in any order
mistakes.what: Tightening the six coolant pump bolts in any order.
mistakes.consequence: The pump is pulled off its locating points and seals unevenly, and its gasket is not sold separately.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten the two locating bolts to their first value, then the other four.

steps.title: Refit the harness and generator
steps.action: Lay the engine harness back on, reconnect every connector, and install the generator.

spec.note: generator bolts

mistakes.title: Leaving a connector unlatched
mistakes.what: Pushing a harness connector on without engaging its latch.
mistakes.consequence: Vibration works the connector loose later, giving intermittent codes that are hard to trace.
mistakes.prevent: Push each connector home until the latch clicks, then tug-test it.

mistakes.title: Leaving harness clips off
mistakes.what: Laying the harness back on without refitting all its clips and brackets.
mistakes.consequence: The harness rubs or sags onto hot turbo and exhaust parts and its insulation melts.
mistakes.prevent: Refit every clip and bracket following your removal photos.

steps.title: Fit idlers and accessory belt
steps.action: Refit each idler pulley to its noted position and fit the accessory belt.

spec.note: M10 idler bolt; M8 idler bolt 25 N·m

steps.mistake: Swapping the two idler pulleys between positions.

mistakes.title: Swapping the idler pulleys
mistakes.what: Refitting the two idler pulleys in each other's positions.
mistakes.consequence: Each position takes a different bolt size, so a bolt is wrong for its hole or gets the wrong torque.
mistakes.prevent: Refit each idler to its labeled position with its own bolt.

steps.title: Refit pipes, dipstick tube and pads
steps.action: Install the coolant pipes, degas bottle, breather, purge valve, dipstick tube and NVH pads with new or inspected O-rings.

mistakes.title: Forgetting the NVH pads
mistakes.what: Leaving off the foam and laminate NVH pads.
mistakes.consequence: The engine is noticeably louder in the cabin than before the rebuild.
mistakes.prevent: Refit each pad in the place it came from.

steps.title: Install engine and transmission
steps.action: Mate the engine to the ZF 9HP48 transmission and refit the powertrain to the vehicle following the vehicle procedures.

mistakes.title: Bolting up with the converter unseated
mistakes.what: Pulling the engine and transmission together on the bellhousing bolts with the converter not fully engaged.
mistakes.consequence: The converter is forced against the transmission pump and can break it as the bolts are tightened.
mistakes.prevent: Check that the converter is fully seated and that the housings meet by hand before fitting any bolt.

steps.title: Fill with approved 0W-20
steps.action: Fill with 0W-20 oil meeting STJLR.51.5122 and check the level on the dipstick.
steps.why: JLR warns that oil outside its specification can make the CVVL system malfunction.

spec.note: approximate refill with filter; set final level on the dipstick

steps.mistake: Using a generic 5W-30, which the CVVL hydraulics are not calibrated for.

mistakes.title: Filling with a generic 5W-30
mistakes.what: Filling the engine with a general-purpose 5W-30.
mistakes.consequence: JLR warns that oil outside its specification can make the CVVL system malfunction.
mistakes.prevent: Fill only with 0W-20 that meets STJLR.51.5122.

mistakes.title: Using an unapproved 0W-20
mistakes.what: Using a 0W-20 oil that does not carry the JLR approval.
mistakes.consequence: The oil may not have the additive package JLR approved for this engine's sludge-prone high-pressure circuits.
mistakes.prevent: Check the label for STJLR.51.5122, not just the viscosity.

mistakes.title: Overfilling to the book capacity
mistakes.what: Pouring in the full capacity figure without checking the dipstick.
mistakes.consequence: Too much oil is churned by the crank, aerating it and raising crankcase pressure.
mistakes.prevent: Fill a little short, run the priming routine, then set the final level on the dipstick.

steps.title: Vacuum fill the cooling system
steps.action: Vacuum fill the cooling system and check for leaks at the pump, thermostat housing, oil cooler and turbo lines.

mistakes.title: Gravity filling the cooling system
mistakes.what: Pouring in coolant without a vacuum fill.
mistakes.consequence: Air pockets trapped in the head and turbo passages cause hot spots and can overheat the head.
mistakes.prevent: Use a vacuum filler, then check for leaks at the pump, housing, cooler and turbo pipes.

steps.title: Run the CVVL calibration
steps.action: Connect JLR-approved diagnostic equipment and run the CVVL software calibration.
steps.why: JLR requires this after any CVVL removal or replacement so the PCM learns the unit's switching behavior.
steps.mistake: Starting the engine and skipping the calibration, which leaves the engine misfiring or in limp mode.

mistakes.title: Skipping the CVVL calibration
mistakes.what: Starting the engine without running the CVVL software calibration.
mistakes.consequence: The PCM does not know the unit's switching behavior, so the engine misfires or goes into limp mode.
mistakes.prevent: Run the JLR CVVL calibration with approved equipment before first start.

steps.title: Crank to build oil pressure
steps.action: Unplug the injector harness and crank for 10 seconds, rest 5 seconds, and repeat 4 times so oil fills the CVVL unit, phasers and turbo before firing.

spec.note: crank 10 s, rest 5 s, repeat 4 times, injectors unplugged

steps.mistake: Letting the engine fire on the first crank with dry CVVL chambers and turbo bearings.

mistakes.title: Letting the engine fire on first crank
mistakes.what: Cranking the engine with the injectors connected so it fires straight away.
mistakes.consequence: The CVVL chambers, phasers and turbo bearings work before oil has reached them.
