mistakes.prevent: Unplug the injectors and complete the full cranking routine before starting.

mistakes.title: Cranking past ten seconds
mistakes.what: Holding the starter on continuously instead of in 10-second bursts.
mistakes.consequence: The starter overheats and battery voltage sags during the CVVL priming routine.
mistakes.prevent: Crank 10 seconds, rest 5 seconds, four times, as specified.

mistakes.title: Not rechecking the oil after priming
mistakes.what: Skipping the oil level check after the priming cranks.
mistakes.consequence: Oil has moved into the filter, cooler and CVVL unit, so the engine may start low on oil.
mistakes.prevent: Recheck the dipstick after priming and top up before starting.

steps.title: Reconnect injectors and clear codes
steps.action: Reconnect the injector harness and clear any stored codes with the diagnostic tool.

mistakes.title: Clearing codes without reading them
mistakes.what: Clearing codes stored during priming without reading them.
mistakes.consequence: A real fault, such as an unplugged sensor or CVVL solenoid, is wiped and only found later.
mistakes.prevent: Read and record every code, fix any not caused by the unplugged injectors, then clear them.

steps.title: Idle for one minute
steps.action: Start the engine and let it idle for at least one minute without revving, so the CVVL unit reaches full oil pressure.
steps.mistake: Revving the engine right after first start.

mistakes.title: Revving straight after first start
mistakes.what: Revving the engine as soon as it fires.
mistakes.consequence: The CVVL unit has not reached full oil pressure, so its chambers and brake units take load while half full.
mistakes.prevent: Idle for at least a minute without touching the throttle.

mistakes.title: Idling with the oil pressure warning on
mistakes.what: Leaving the engine idling while the oil pressure warning stays on.
mistakes.consequence: Bearings, phasers and the CVVL unit run without oil and can be wiped out in seconds.
mistakes.prevent: Switch off at once if the warning stays on, and find the cause before restarting.

steps.title: Inspect for leaks and noise
steps.action: With the engine idling, check the HP fuel unions, injector seals, turbo oil lines and coolant joints, and listen for chain rattle at the transmission end.
steps.why: A rattle from the rear on a fresh engine means a tensioner or phaser problem; shut down at once.

mistakes.title: Ignoring a rattle at the timing end
mistakes.what: Putting a rattle from the transmission end on first start down to new parts settling.
mistakes.consequence: A tensioner or phaser fault left running can let the chain jump teeth and hit valves.
mistakes.prevent: Shut down at once and check the tensioners, phasers and timing before running it again.

mistakes.title: Not checking HP unions under pressure
mistakes.what: Checking the HP fuel unions only with the engine off.
mistakes.consequence: A seep that only shows at direct-injection pressure goes unnoticed until it is a fire risk.
mistakes.prevent: Inspect every HP union and injector seal with a light while the engine idles.

steps.title: Plan an early oil change
steps.action: Change the oil and filter early after the rebuild, and recommend shorter intervals to owners who drive mostly short urban trips.
steps.why: JLR found that hard urban driving degrades oil fast enough to sludge the CVVL and high-pressure galleries, and runs early oil-change campaigns for it.

mistakes.title: Skipping the early oil change
mistakes.what: Leaving the first oil change after the rebuild to the normal interval.
mistakes.consequence: Assembly lube and fine debris stay in the oil and degrade it in the circuits feeding the CVVL unit.
mistakes.prevent: Change the oil and filter early after the rebuild and shorten intervals for urban use.

mistakes.title: Resetting the service interval
mistakes.what: Resetting the service reminder after the extra early oil change.
mistakes.consequence: The next full service, which covers far more than oil, comes due later than it should.
mistakes.prevent: Leave the service interval alone after an extra oil change, as JLR instructs.

failureModes.title: Intake VCT actuator internal seal leak
failureModes.cause: An internal seal in the intake VCT actuator can be below specification, so the phaser cannot hold its position on oil pressure.
symptoms: Rattle from the timing chain area at the rear of the engine
Check engine light (MIL) on with P052A-00, P0011-71 or P000A-00 stored
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Fit the current intake VCT actuator with a new center bolt (ingenium-pt204-044, -138) and a new secondary tensioner (ingenium-pt204-143), clean the phaser feed bores (ingenium-pt204-081), and only torque the bolts after the tensioner has released with the locking tools fitted (ingenium-pt204-144, -145).

failureModes.title: VCT solenoid faults
failureModes.cause: The original VCT solenoids on 2018 to 2020 engines can misbehave, and JLR replaces both under service action N481.
symptoms: Flat spots when driving
Check engine light (MIL) with VCT codes stored
More induction noise and slightly less performance
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Check the VIN for N481, fit the current solenoids on new O-rings in oiled bores (ingenium-pt204-154), and keep the solenoid bores clean while the engine is apart (ingenium-pt204-031).

failureModes.title: Oil degradation and sludge in high-pressure circuits
failureModes.cause: Hard urban drive cycles degrade the oil faster than the service interval allows, leaving sludge in the high-pressure galleries and inside the CVVL unit.
symptoms: Sludge in the old oil and around the filler
CVVL misfires or VCT faults that follow sludge buildup
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Sample the old oil (ingenium-pt204-002), clean every high-pressure gallery and the oil cooler (ingenium-pt204-080), judge the CVVL unit strictly (ingenium-pt204-094), fill with approved 0W-20 (ingenium-pt204-180) and change the oil early (ingenium-pt204-187).

failureModes.title: CVVL unit failure and misfire
failureModes.cause: The sealed electrohydraulic CVVL unit stops switching intake valve lift correctly, often linked to degraded oil, and can only be replaced as a unit.
symptoms: Poor idle or rough running
Check engine light (MIL) with P1315, P0316 or P0300
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Replace a suspect unit (ingenium-pt204-094), keep it upright and clean (ingenium-pt204-056), reset the brake units and fit it by the pilot bolt method (ingenium-pt204-155, -156), then calibrate, prime and idle it as JLR specifies (ingenium-pt204-182, -183, -185).

failureModes.title: Timing chain, guide and tensioner wear
failureModes.cause: The two chains at the transmission end wear along with their plastic guides and hydraulic tensioners, letting the drive go slack.
failureModes.symptoms: Rattle from the rear of the engine, worst at start-up, often with cam timing codes.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Renew both chains, all guides and both tensioners (ingenium-pt204-133 to -143), make sure each tensioner is actually released (ingenium-pt204-135, -144), and check the timing over two turns by hand (ingenium-pt204-147).

failureModes.title: Valve damage after lost timing
failureModes.cause: This is an interference engine, so a jumped chain or mistimed rebuild lets pistons hit open valves.
symptoms: Low compression on one or more cylinders
Misfire or no-start after a rattle or a timing job
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Compression-test before teardown (ingenium-pt204-003), turn the engine only clockwise and never with the chains off (ingenium-pt204-037, -052), set the crank before the cams (ingenium-pt204-131) and hand-turn check before closing up (ingenium-pt204-147).

failureModes.title: Injector seal fuel leak
failureModes.cause: Injector seals that are reused, damaged or fitted in the wrong order leak fuel or combustion gas; JLR found the Bosch sheet in its refit kit gave the wrong order.
symptoms: Fuel smell or a leak under the hood
Ticking or a combustion leak at an injector
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Fit new seals following the JLR procedure, not the Bosch sheet, size them correctly, and seat the rail on its guide pins one turn at a time (ingenium-pt204-030, -163, -164).

failureModes.title: High-pressure fuel line leak
failureModes.cause: An HP line tightened more times than allowed, or not rechecked after first tightening, stops sealing at direct-injection pressure.
failureModes.symptoms: Fuel smell and a wet union at the pump or rail, a fire risk on a hot engine.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Count the paint marks on removal (ingenium-pt204-024), tighten, wait and recheck each union and paint-mark it (ingenium-pt204-167), then inspect the unions with the engine running (ingenium-pt204-186).

failureModes.title: Turbocharger failure from oil problems
failureModes.cause: Most turbo failures come from oil starvation or contamination: blocked or damaged pipes, no priming at fitting, or carbon-laden oil.
symptoms: Whine or rising turbo noise
Smoke from oil getting past the turbine seal
Loss of boost
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Protect the oil ports at teardown (ingenium-pt204-017), find why a failed turbo died (ingenium-pt204-093), keep the return clear (ingenium-pt204-172), prime the turbo and fit new feed parts (ingenium-pt204-173), and build oil pressure by cranking before firing (ingenium-pt204-183).

failureModes.title: Bearing failure after a rebuild
failureModes.cause: Dirt left in the engine, oil starvation and misassembly are the main killers of freshly fitted bearings.
symptoms: Knock from the bottom end
Low oil pressure warning
Bearing material in the filter
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Clean the galleries and threads and wash after machining (ingenium-pt204-080, -100), fit shells clean and dry with oil holes aligned (ingenium-pt204-102), get cap order and orientation right (ingenium-pt204-106, -113), and keep RTV out of the pickup (ingenium-pt204-117).

failureModes.title: Blow-by and oil consumption after a rebuild
failureModes.cause: Rings fitted with the wrong gap, upside down or with gaps lined up, or bores left with honing grit, fail to seal.
symptoms: Blue smoke and oil use
Low compression or high crankcase pressure
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Gap every ring for a turbo engine (ingenium-pt204-084), wash the bores after honing (ingenium-pt204-097), fit rings the right way up with gaps 120 degrees apart (ingenium-pt204-110), and fit pistons through a flat compressor (ingenium-pt204-112).

failureModes.title: Oil leaks from sealant joints
failureModes.cause: The oil pan and timing covers leak when their RTV or gaskets are fitted past the open time, out of sequence or on damaged faces.
failureModes.symptoms: Oil seeping from the pan rail or the rear of the engine behind the drive plate.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Clean the faces without abrasives (ingenium-pt204-079), fit the pan and lower cover within their 7-minute windows in sequence (ingenium-pt204-117, -148, -149), and run the upper cover's three-stage torque (ingenium-pt204-153).
